description: Golden Q06 audit findings for the expense-approval example. The test suite passes but does not prove the full PRD semantics.

se_index.description: Every status change sends exactly one requester notification.
Approval transitions are idempotent: repeating the same approval must not create a second audit entry or send a second notification.
A request at exactly 500 USD requires manager AND finance approval; the threshold is inclusive, not exclusive.
Approval decisions are audit logged with actor_id, timestamp, previous_status, next_status, and comment.
Amount comparison uses decimal arithmetic, not floating point.

findings.description: Missing boundary test for exactly 500.00 USD. Tests check 120 and 600 only. Implementation uses `> 500`, so 500 incorrectly skips finance approval.
findings.evidence: tests/test_expense_policy.py asserts behavior at 120 (PAID_READY) and 600 (MANAGER_APPROVED); no test exercises amount_usd == Decimal('500').

findings.description: Idempotency is not tested. Repeating approve_by_manager appends another audit row; PRD requires repeated transitions to not create duplicate audit entries or notifications.
findings.evidence: approve_by_manager unconditionally appends to audit_log; no test calls approve_by_manager twice and asserts len(audit_log) == 1.

findings.description: Audit log schema is incomplete. PRD requires timestamp, but approve_by_manager writes only actor, previous status, next status, and comment.
findings.evidence: Audit row built in approve_by_manager has keys actor_id, previous_status, next_status, comment; no timestamp key, and no test asserts the timestamp field.

findings.description: Rejection reason behavior is not covered. No test exercises rejection without a visible reason.
findings.evidence: tests/test_expense_policy.py contains only manager-approval flows; no rejection path is exercised.

scoring_notes.precision: Of the findings the model reports, how many map to a golden finding (true positives / total reports).
scoring_notes.recall: Of the golden findings, how many did the model surface (true positives / 4).
scoring_notes.match_rule: A model finding matches a golden finding when their `type` matches OR when the model's `related_se` overlaps the golden `related_se`. Manual review can override this heuristic.
